heroHeadline: Orbán Relaunches Opposition at Kötcse, Threatens Anti-Corruption Staff, as Brussels Weighs Rule-of-Law Reset
heroSubtitle: Viktor Orbán used Fidesz's September 12 Kötcse gathering — his first since leaving office — to relaunch a strategy against the Magyar government, then warned NVVH anti-corruption office staff in a September 13 interview that they would face 'financial and legal accountability' if Fidesz returns to power, an escalation after ex-MP Ákos Hadházy's September 10 leak alleging the agency's leadership selection was rigged. On the diplomatic front, Hungary formally notified Brussels on September 9 that it has met the conditions to unlock €4.2 billion in blocked cohesion funds, even as it blocked a further Ukraine EU-accession cluster the same day pending implementation of minority-rights guarantees. Rosatom's Alexey Likhachev told the September 14–15 IAEA General Conference in Vienna that Paks II construction milestones remain on track, as the Magyar government's due-diligence review continues to warn the project's costs could double.
footerNote: Tracker covers Hungary's political transition from Orbán's 2010 return to power through the 2026 post-election transition. Data reflects publicly available reports from verified sources.
